Monday, April 29, 2013 
 116 
 
 
LEGISLATIVE ASSEMBLY OF MANITOBA 
__________________________ 
 
VOTES AND PROCEEDINGS   No. 32 
 
SECOND SESSION, FORTIETH LEGISLATURE 
 
PRAYER 1:30 O'CLOCK P.M. 
 
The following Bills were respectively read a First Time and had their purposes outlined: 
 
(No. 30) – The Forest Health Protection Amendment Act (Heritage Trees)/Loi modifiant la loi sur 
la protection de la santé des forêts (arbres remarquables) 
(Hon. Mr. MACKINTOSH) 
 
(No. 31) – The Workplace Safety and Health Amendment Act/Loi modifiant la Loi sur la sécurité 
et l'hygiène du travail 
(Hon. Ms. HOWARD) 
______________________________ 
 
The following petitions were presented and read: 
 
Mr. GOERTZEN – Legislative Assembly of Manitoba t o urge the Provincial Government to not 
raise the PST without holding a provincial referendum. (M. Nacci, D. Roberts, C. Graham and others) 
 
Mr. EWASKO – Legislative Assembly of Manitoba to request that the Minister of Infrastructure 
and Transportation recognize that Cape Coppermine Road can no longer adequately serve both area 
residents and tourists and as such consider making improvements to the road to reflect its current use. 
(L. Penner, A. Penner, C. Radwanski and others) 
 
Mr. PEDERSEN – Legislative Assembly of Manitoba to request that the Minister of Local 
Government afford local governments the respect they deserve and reverse his decision to force 
municipalities with fewer than 1,000 constituents to amalgamate. ( R. Sharpe, B. Fansher, L. Hedley and 
others) 
 
Mr. GRAYDON – Legislative Assembly of Manitoba to urge the Minister of Infrastructure and 
Transportation to repair or replace the existing bridge as soon as possible to allow communities on both 
sides of the river to return to regular activities. (J. Bird, L. Barnabe, E. Dupuis and others) 
______________________________ 
 
Hon. Mr. ASHTON, the Minister responsible for Emergency Measures, made a statement 
regarding the status of flooding in Manitoba.

Mr. EICHLER and, by leave, Hon. Mr. GERRARD commented on the statement.

During Oral Questions, Mr. GOERTZEN rose on a point of order regarding quality of answers 
provided by the Ministers in question period. 
 
And Hon. Mr. ASHTON having spoken to the point of order, 
 
WHEREUPON Mr. Speaker ruled that there was no point of order. 
 
From his decision, Mr. GOERTZEN appealed to the House, 
 
And the Question being put, "Shall the ruling of the Chair be sustained?"  It was agreed to, on th e 
following division:
